question: A class teacher conducted a unit test in the class. If out of 30 students, 14 students scored 80 and rest 16 students scored 65, then what is the weighted average score?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the deviation method with assumed average = 65:

Deviation of 14 students = 80 − 65 = +15

Total deviation = 14 × 15 = +210

Average deviation for all 30 students = +210 ÷ 30 = +7

Weighted average = 65 + 7 = 72

**∴ The correct answer is 72 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Total number of students = 30

⇒ Number of students who scored 80 (N₁) = 14

⇒ Number of students who scored 65 (N₂) = 16

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Weighted Average = (N₁A₁ + N₂A₂) ÷ (N₁ + N₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total score of first group = 14 × 80 = 1120

⇒ Total score of second group = 16 × 65 = 1040

⇒ Overall total score = 1120 + 1040 = 2160

⇒ Weighted Average = 2160 ÷ 30 = 72

**∴ The correct answer is 72 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

Used when different data points contribute unequally to the final average. Formula: Aw = (w₁x₁ + w₂x₂) ÷ (w₁ + w₂).

Deviation Method

An assumed mean is selected to reduce calculation. True Average = Assumed Mean + (Sum of Deviations ÷ Total Frequency).

Alligation Approach for Averages

The ratio of the quantities in two groups is inversely proportional to the difference between their individual averages and the combined average.
